inputs.proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.
inputs.original_proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.

questions: Does the removal of the core initialization check in QML files imply that all UI elements that previously depended on coreInitialized will now behave differently when the core is not initialized? This could lead to unexpected behavior if the underlying core functions are still being called without proper initialization.

Are there any potential race conditions or thread safety issues introduced by removing the coreInitialized flag from QtTuneBridge and its associated QML bindings, especially considering that ecuio_init() is now a no-op?

The change in core.h comments mentions that sessions, profile registry and discovery work without ecuio_init. Is there any guarantee that calling functions like ecuio_session_create or ecuio_profile_lookup will behave consistently when the core has never been initialized?
nits: Consider adding a comment to ecuio_init() in core.cpp explaining why it's now a no-op, especially since this change might not be obvious to someone reading the code without context.
In QtTuneBridge::QtTuneBridge(), the line (void)ecuio_init(); could benefit from a comment explaining that this is intentional as init is now always ECUIO_OK and does nothing.

The removal of coreInitializedChanged() signal in QtTuneBridge might break existing code that relies on this signal for UI updates or other logic. While the QML changes have been updated to remove dependency, it's worth confirming no external consumers are relying on this signal.
